title: 第四章 浮生荣华

content_zh:
冯元吉与老王爷是多年的交情，他又是个不拘俗礼的人，踏星而来祭奠故人，倒露了些许这虚情假意的年头里，难能一见的真情来。
想不到这一世，倒是能见他离京前的最后一面。
见问，景七倏地一笑：“我好歹是太子侍读，如今太子已经到了听朝的年纪，大大小小的事，虽不该我听，好歹也知道一些。”
冯元吉“嘿”地一笑，叫景七一句话无意点中心事，那一刻脸上的悲愤之意，竟连收都收不住，只是他自来是个刚硬汉子，不愿在这稚子少年面前流露，当下只是扭过头去，望着灵堂外暗淡天色，沉默半晌，才控制住声音神色，压着嗓子，尽量平静地说道：“连你一个小娃子心里都记挂的事，该听的人却偏偏听不见。”
可怜夜半虚前席，不问苍生问鬼神。
景七眉心一跳，还未来得及开口，却见冯元吉转过头来，沉声道：“这话我说出口本是不该，你便当做没听见，知道么？”
灵堂里白烛随着微风微微闪烁，火盆里烧着半张纸钱，那少年的脸色也仿似凭空借了几分火气，静静地坐在那，一双眼睛点漆似的，深深地望过来，竟像是他什么都知道一样。冯元吉看得心下忍不住一软。
他当景北渊是半个子侄，眼下景明哲撂了挑子，他又要远走南疆，这一去不知是生是死，只觉这早熟聪慧的少年披麻戴孝地在灵堂里的样子，分外单薄孤寂。
于是放柔了嗓音：“南疆叛乱，皇上方下旨令我平乱，此去……此去恐怕天长路远，我不在京中，照应不得你，你好自为之。”顿了顿，到底不放心，又叮嘱道，“我知道你向来与太子亲厚，太子也是个好样的，只是……”
冯元吉虽然书读得不多，到底在官场摸爬滚打了几十年，说这话时将吐未吐，景七却明白了他的意思，当今皇上看似春秋正盛，不过是个被声色掏空了身子的花架子，这江山尚不知谁来做主，到时候三位皇子有得好斗，冯大将军这是怕自己搅合进这摊烂泥里。
景七轻轻一笑，往火盆里添了些许纸钱：“我不过靠着祖荫顶着虚名的一个闲散王爷，又是个黄口小儿，养在这帝都里，偶尔给皇伯父些承欢膝下的乐儿，在诸位大人眼里，跟上书房那‘督察御史’大人一路货色，好好儿的谁还把我当回事？大将军多虑了。”
那“督察御史”大人便是眼下皇上最宠的、把文武百官都差不多骂过一遭的八哥鸟，可冯元吉听着这孩子似讥带讽言语，心里却一沉，心道他才多大的人，便有这般思虑？
端详着他低眉轻笑的模样，悠悠沉沉，竟没有半分少年模样。
景七道：“我是不妨事，将军可知，南疆一战，乃是死局？”
冯元吉心下一震，忍不住脱口问道：“怎讲？”
“南疆虽小，可自当年□□得天下，趟平九州而朝昔日同列时起，这块地方便如骨鲠在吼，太宗好武，在位三十六年，两回北征，叫那北漠蛮人俯首称臣，却到底饮恨南州，英雄末路。南疆之地多山多恶水，瘴气密林，行路不便先放在一边，但是我中原将士们水土不服便够喝一壶的，何况……”
自然不用他讲史，冯元吉接到圣旨那刻开始，便抱了死志，只未想到被这少年说了出来，不由打断他道：“这话是谁教你的？”
景七随口搪塞：“周太傅。”
冯元吉摇摇头，太傅周自逸名字叫得飘逸，却是第一等古板的人，开口三句不离圣人言，断断不会和孩子妄议当朝之事，况且他一介书生，酸腐文人，也不见得就懂得这征战之中道理。
景七但笑不语。

冯元吉有心听他说，便道：“你继续说下去。”
景七却有些费力地起身，一动，头还是有些昏沉，勉力稳住身形，站起来把灵堂的门合上，又坐回原位，像是干了重活似的长长舒出口气来，缓一缓，才压低声音道：“当今圣上耽于玩乐，看似荒唐，心里也不是不虚的……”
话还没说完，冯元吉便厉声喝道：“当今圣上可是你妄议的？这话大逆不道！”

content_en:
Feng Yuanji had been friends with the old prince for many years, and he was a person who was informal in etiquette. He came to pay homage to his old friend, revealing a bit of true love that was rare to see in these years of false love.
Unexpectedly, in this life, I would be able to see him for the last time before leaving Beijing.
When asked, Jing Qi smiled suddenly: "I am the prince's attendant after all. Now the prince has reached the age of listening to the court. Although I should not hear about big and small things, I still know some things."
Feng Yuanji smiled "hey" and told Jing Qi that he had no intention of getting to the point. At that moment, he couldn't even hold back the sadness and anger on his face. However, he was always a tough guy and didn't want to show it in front of this childish boy. At that moment, he could only He turned his head and looked at the dim sky outside the mourning hall. After a long silence, he controlled his voice and expression, lowered his voice and said as calmly as possible: "Even a little kid like you is worried about things, but the people who should hear them can't hear them."
It's a pity that I sit down at the front table in the middle of the night and don't ask about the common people or the ghosts and gods.
Jing Qi's eyebrows twitched, but before she could speak, Feng Yuanji turned his head and said in a deep voice, "I shouldn't have said this, so just pretend you didn't hear it, you know?"
In the mourning hall, the white candles flickered slightly with the breeze, and half a piece of paper money was burning in the brazier. The young man's face seemed to have borrowed some fire out of thin air. He sat there quietly, with his eyes like paint, looking deeply at him, as if he knew everything. Feng Yuanji couldn't help but feel soft in his heart.
He regarded Jing Beiyuan as his half-nephew, and now that Jing Mingzhe had given up his plans, he was leaving for southern Xinjiang again. He didn't know whether he was going to live or die, but he felt that this precocious and intelligent young man was extremely lonely and lonely in the mourning hall wearing sackcloth and mourning.
So he softened his voice and said, "There is a rebellion in southern Xinjiang. The emperor ordered me to quell the rebellion. I'm afraid it's a long way to go... I'm not in the capital, so I can't take care of you. You can take care of yourself." After a pause, he felt uneasy, and then warned, "I know you have always been close to the prince, and the prince is also a good person, but..."
Although Feng Yuanji didn't read many books, he had been in the officialdom for decades. When he said this, he was about to spit out his words, but Jing Qi understood what he meant. The emperor seemed to be in his prime, but he was just a showman whose body was hollowed out by appearance. It was still unclear who would make the final decision in this country. The three princes would be aggressive when the time came, and General Feng was afraid that he would get involved in this mess.
Jing Qi smiled softly and added some paper money into the brazier: "I am just an idle prince who relies on the shadow of my ancestors for a false reputation. I am also a child with a yellow mouth. I am raised in this imperial capital and occasionally give the emperor some entertainment. In the eyes of you adults, I am just like the 'Inspector Yushi' in the study. Who will take me seriously? The general is worrying too much."
The "Inspector and Censor" is the emperor's favorite at the moment, and he has scolded all the civil and military officials. But Feng Yuanji's heart sank when he heard the child's sarcastic words. How old was he to have such thoughts?
Looking at his lowered eyebrows and chuckle, he looked serious and did not look like a teenager at all.
Jing Qi said: "I don't care. Does the general know that a battle in southern Xinjiang will be a dead end?"
Feng Yuanji was shocked and couldn't help but blurted out: "How to say?"
"Although the southern frontier is small, since the time when the emperor conquered the world and conquered the nine states and returned to the same line in the past, this land has been roaring like a bone. Taizong was fond of martial arts. During his thirty-sixth year in power, he made two expeditions to the north, making the northern desert barbarians bow their heads. He proclaimed himself a vassal, but he hated Nanzhou, and the hero was doomed. The southern frontier is mountainous, has bad water, and is filled with miasma and dense forests. Putting aside the inconvenience of traveling, our Central Plains soldiers are not accustomed to the acclimatization and can drink a pot of it, not to mention..."
Naturally, there was no need for him to talk about history. From the moment Feng Yuanji received the imperial edict, he was determined to die. He didn't expect that this young man would say it, so he couldn't help but interrupt him: "Who taught you this?"
Jing Qi casually prevaricates: "Teacher Zhou."
Feng YuanJi shook his head. The Taifu Zhou Ziyi had an elegant name, but he was a first-class old-fashioned person. He always spoke the words of a sage and would never talk to his children about the affairs of the day. Moreover, he was a scholar and a corrupt scholar, so he did not necessarily understand the principles of war.
Jing Qi smiled but said nothing.
Feng Yuanji was interested in listening to what he said and said, "You continue."
Jing Qi got up with some effort. His head was still a little dizzy when he moved. He tried his best to steady his body, stood up and closed the door of the mourning hall, then sat back down. He let out a long breath as if he had done a heavy job. After a while, he lowered his voice and said: "Today's Holy Emperor is obsessed with having fun. It seems ridiculous, but he is not guilty at heart..."
Before he finished speaking, Feng Yuanji shouted sternly: "Is this what you, the Holy One, are talking about? This is treason!"
